newsitem.title: BRAZIL: New Brazil sugar results confirm slowdown - DataNet.
newsitem.headline: New Brazil sugar results confirm slowdown - DataNet.

text.p: The latest set of figures in Brazilian sugar production in the center-south confirm a seasonal deceleration in production growth, said independent consultants DataNet-Agricommodities.

Results from the eleventh fortnightly period to October 1 means that total 1996/97 center-south sugar production is now running at a 3.9 perent increase from the corresponding period last year, DataNet said.
This is down from peak growth of 6.4 percent at the end of the ninth period to September 1 but is better than the 1.9 percent growth registered by September 16.
"According to surveys carried out by DataNet, the low levels seen in the tenth period were due to rains last month which reduced the number of crushing days," DataNet said.
"However the figures confirm a seasonal slowdown on production growth," it added.

Sugar production by the end of the eleventh period reached 8.04 million tonnes against 7.74 million tonnes in the corresponding period in the 1995/96 campaign which was up to October 16 given this year's harvest began two weeks earlier.
Sugar production by October 1, 1995 was 6.96 million tonnes, according to statistics from the Sao Paulo Association of Sugar and Alcohol Industries.
Cane crushings rose 4.4 percent to 176.45 million tonnes by the end of the eleventh period against 168.95 million tonnes in the corresponding two-week period in 1995/96, DataNet said.
